title: A Mentor for the Next Step
transcript: When I joined a packaging company as an intern, my supervisor paired me with a senior designer because we had studied at the same college. We got along well, and she gave detailed feedback on my sketches. My project, though, involved finding out why certain packages jammed on a sealing machine. She rarely worked on the production floor, so our meetings produced very few leads. My supervisor arranged for me to spend Friday mornings with a machine technician. He showed me how to check whether the trays arrived at the sealer at a consistent angle. I still took revised sketches to the designer before sending them to production.

questions.prompt: Why did the early meetings yield few leads for the project?
options: The designer had little direct experience in the production area.
The intern had been unable to obtain the original sketches.
The supervisor had assigned two unrelated projects.
The faulty packages had already been thrown away.
questions.answer: The designer had little direct experience in the production area.
questions.explanation: 项目需要排查生产线上的卡机问题，而设计师很少到生产现场。

questions.prompt: How did the two colleagues support the intern by the end?
options: They took turns operating the sealing machine.
They jointly chose a new project for the intern.
They helped with different parts of the same assignment.
questions.answer: They helped with different parts of the same assignment.
questions.explanation: 技术员帮助排查机器问题，设计师继续审阅修改后的草图。

section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
